title: Buyer's Guide to NYC Real Estate
subtitle: Your comprehensive guide to purchasing property in New York City

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.content:
Buying property in New York City is an exciting journey that requires preparation and knowledge. This guide will walk you through the process from initial planning to closing day.

**First Steps:**
- Assess your financial readiness
- Get pre-approved for a mortgage
- Define your priorities (location, size, amenities)
- Understand the difference between co-ops and condos

sections.title: Understanding NYC Property Types
sections.content:
### Condominiums (Condos)
You own your individual unit as real property. Generally easier approval process, more flexibility with subletting and renovations. Higher purchase prices but lower monthly common charges.

### Cooperatives (Co-ops)
You purchase shares in a corporation that owns the building. Typically 20-30% less expensive than condos but stricter approval processes and subletting policies. Often require higher down payments (20-50%).

### Townhouses
Multi-story buildings you own outright, including the land. Rare in Manhattan, more common in Brooklyn and Queens. Full control but full responsibility for maintenance.

sections.title: The Buying Process
sections.content:
### 1. Get Pre-Approved
Speak with lenders to understand your budget and get a pre-approval letter. This shows sellers you're a serious buyer.

### 2. Find Your Property
Work with a buyer's agent to search listings, attend open houses, and identify properties that meet your criteria.

### 3. Make an Offer
Submit an offer including price, contingencies, and proposed timeline. Negotiations may follow.

### 4. Due Diligence
Once under contract, conduct inspections, review building financials (for co-ops/condos), and finalize your mortgage.

### 5. Board Approval (Co-ops/Some Condos)
Prepare and submit your application package. Attend board interview if required.

### 6. Closing
Sign final documents, transfer funds, and receive your keys!

sections.title: Financial Considerations
sections.content:
### Down Payment
- Condos: Typically 10-20% minimum
- Co-ops: Often 20-50% required
- First-time buyer programs may offer lower requirements

### Closing Costs
Budget 2-5% of purchase price for:
- Attorney fees ($2,000-4,000)
- Title insurance
- Mortgage recording tax
- Mansion tax (purchases over $1M)
- Transfer taxes

### Monthly Costs
- Mortgage payment
- Common charges or maintenance fees
- Property taxes (condos/townhouses)
- Homeowner's insurance

sections.title: Working with a Buyer's Agent
sections.content:
A buyer's agent represents your interests exclusively throughout the purchase process.

**Benefits include:**
- Access to listings and market knowledge
- Negotiation expertise
- Guidance through complex paperwork
- Coordination with attorneys, lenders, and other parties
- No direct cost to you (commission typically paid by seller)

At Mallan Real Estate, our agents bring deep NYC expertise and a commitment to finding you the right property at the right price.

sections.title: Tips for Success
sections.content:
- **Be prepared to act quickly** - Good properties move fast in NYC
- **Know your non-negotiables** - But be flexible on nice-to-haves
- **Research the neighborhood** - Visit at different times of day
- **Review building financials** - Look for healthy reserves and stable fees
- **Get everything in writing** - Verbal agreements aren't binding
- **Work with experienced professionals** - Attorney, agent, and lender all matter
